children: Cantor Fitzgerald raised its price target on Snowflake

to $405 from $282, keeping an Overweight rating, two days before the company reports fiscal second quarter results. That sits above every other target in the recent range. Snowflake shares were down 0.93% intraday.

Cantor pointed to expanding software multiples, particularly for companies tied to agentic and data-driven demand. On the quarter itself the firm is more measured, expecting product revenue to beat the guidance midpoint by more than 3% against 5.5% last quarter. Channel checks still point to a beat-and-raise, with Cortex Code adoption holding through the period and core usage steady.

Cantor tied the momentum to cloud migrations and consolidation of data layer spend, and flagged what it sees as the swing factor: whether incremental AI consumption more than offsets optimization coming out of those consolidations. Others have moved ahead of the print too, with Benchmark at $360, TD Cowen at $370, and Morgan Stanley reiterating Overweight at $300. The options market implies a move of about 12% on the results.

title: Cantor Lifts Snowflake Target to $405 Two Days Before Earnings
